Q: How do lexical retrieval, dense retrieval and cross-encoder reranking complement one another?
A: Lexical retrieval rewards token matches under a scoring model, dense retrieval compares learned representations, and a cross-encoder jointly scores a query/candidate pair. They fail differently: identifiers can favor exact matching, paraphrases can favor dense representations, and joint scoring can improve ordering of a bounded candidate set. A reranker cannot recover a relevant item absent from that set. Fuse or combine ranks under an evaluated policy rather than directly averaging incompatible raw score scales. Apply authorization consistently before evidence is exposed.
Why: A product code can be missed by a dense encoder while a paraphrased question misses lexical terms. Taking authorized candidates from both can improve coverage before a more expensive reranker selects a small final set.
Risk: A better reranker may leave candidate-recall failures unchanged.
Trade: Spend expensive scoring on candidates with demonstrated coverage value.
Try: Separate candidate recall from final ranking quality for exact-code and paraphrase queries.
